cards.text: Picture the house of the LORD, with worshipers coming in from all the cities of Judah. It's the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, and the LORD gives His prophet Jeremiah a message for every one of them. Jeremiah is to stand right there in the courtyard and deliver it.

cards.question: Before Jeremiah goes, the LORD adds one more instruction about His message. What is it?

answers.text: Don't leave out a single word
Write it on a scroll first

cards.question: The LORD tells Jeremiah there's no chance the people of Judah will listen to His message.

cards.text: Perhaps. The LORD says perhaps they'll listen and turn from their evil ways, and He may relent of the disaster He's planning.

Then comes the warning: if they won't listen to the LORD and walk in His law, or listen to the prophets He has sent them again and again, something is coming. Sent again and again and still not heard, like an alarm that goes off every morning and gets the snooze button EVERY time.
If they won't listen, the LORD says He will make His house like Shiloh, the place where He first made a dwelling for His Name (Jeremiah 7:12).

cards.question: If the people won't listen, the LORD says He will make this city an object of ___ among all the nations of the earth.

cards.text: The priests, the prophets and all the people hear Jeremiah say it, right there in the house of the LORD. He gets through EVERYTHING the LORD commanded him to say, not one word skipped.

cards.question: The second Jeremiah finishes, what do the priests, the prophets and the people do?

answers.text: Seize him and shout for his death
Tear their clothes and cry out
Turn and walk out in silence

cards.question: The crowd shouts at Jeremiah. They say he dared to prophesy in the name of the LORD that this city would end up how?

cards.text: All the people gather against Jeremiah in the LORD's house, and when the officials of Judah hear about it, they come up from the king's palace. You know it's serious when the bosses leave the corner office.
They sit down at the entrance of the New Gate, and court is now in session. The priests and prophets tell the officials and all the people that this man is worthy of death.

cards.question: The priests and prophets say the officials and the people already know what Jeremiah said. How do they know?

answers.text: They heard it with their own ears
The king read it out to them
A scribe wrote it down for them

cards.question: The priests and prophets give their reason: Jeremiah prophesied against the city.

cards.text: Back at the New Gate, it's Jeremiah's turn to speak to the officials and all the people. He tells them straight: the LORD sent him to prophesy every word they heard against this house and this city.

cards.question: With his life on the line, what does Jeremiah urge the officials and the people to do?

answers.text: Correct their ways and obey the LORD
Let him go and forget his words
Take his case before the king

cards.text: Then Jeremiah says, "As for me, here I am in your hands; do to me what you think is good and right." Friend, if a crowd was yelling for ME, I'd be hopping out of there so fast my gold base would leave sparks.

cards.question: Jeremiah warns them that if they put him to death, they'll bring ___ blood on themselves and on the city.
The officials and all the people give their answer to the priests and prophets. What is it?

answers.text: This man is not worthy of death
This man must leave the city
This man must face the king

cards.text: Their reason: he has spoken to them in the name of the LORD their God. And WAIT, the people were shouting for his death, and now they flip faster than a light switch!
Then some of the elders of the land stand up and speak to the whole assembly. They bring up Micah the Moreshite, a prophet back in the days of Hezekiah, king of Judah.

cards.question: What did Micah tell all the people of Judah that the LORD of Hosts says?

answers.text: Zion will be plowed like a field
Zion will never be shaken again
Zion will be crowned with glory

cards.question: King Hezekiah had Micah put to death for that prophecy.

cards.text: Instead, the elders say, Hezekiah feared the LORD and sought His favor, and the LORD relented of the disaster He had pronounced. Same kind of message, totally different ending.

cards.question: The elders warn the assembly that they are about to bring great harm on themselves.

cards.text: Now here's a different story with the same message. Another man, Uriah son of Shemaiah from Kiriath-jearim, was prophesying in the name of the LORD, saying the same things against this city and land that Jeremiah did.

cards.question: King Jehoiakim and all his mighty men and officials hear Uriah's words. What does the king try to do?
When Uriah finds out what the king wants, he flees in ___ and goes to Egypt.

cards.text: But Jehoiakim sends men all the way to Egypt: Elnathan son of Achbor, along with some others. They bring Uriah out of Egypt and take him to King Jehoiakim.
Jehoiakim has Uriah put to the sword, and his body is thrown into the burial place of the common people. So what happens to Jeremiah, who prophesied the very same things?

cards.question: Jeremiah's life is still on the line. Who supports him?

cards.text: Because Ahikam supports him, Jeremiah is not handed over to the people to be put to death. Friend, THAT is the name you want saved at the top of your contacts.
